full_prompt:
Create exactly ONE new original Small Seal script glyph based on the attached four-specimen Unicode reference. THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC are all variants of THE SAME ONE CHARACTER, not separate output characters. Compare ALL available specimens equally to understand the exact identity. Choose ONE coherent attested WHOLE construction if variants differ; never splice incompatible alternatives or default to THX alone. Do not substitute a modern Chinese character.

Trace genuine writing-stroke trajectories as smooth controlled centerline curves. Draw these with exactly CONSTANT uniform thickness approximately 3% of the square canvas width, perfectly rounded caps and joins. No swelling, taper, pointed tips, brush pressure, serif, texture or outline of brush silhouettes. Keep essential branches, short marks, counters, attachments, separations and relative bar lengths explicit. Important small gaps must stay open.

ONE finished glyph centered in the central 70% of a square canvas with generous clear margins. Pure BLACK strokes on fully TRANSPARENT background. No text, labels, charts, grids, frame, four variants, reference copies, shadows, paper, backdrop, ornament or watermark. The structural reading aid below guides attention, while all four reference specimens remain the visual authority.

CHARACTER U+3D045. REVISED reading aid with essential bent returns: IMPORTANT DETAIL: The middle contains TWO SMALL U-TURN STROKES, not dashes. The UPPER small stroke is shaped like ⊃: two visibly SEPARATE PARALLEL HORIZONTAL LEGS, open on the LEFT, connected by a semicircular bend at RIGHT. The LOWER small stroke is shaped like ⊂: two visibly SEPARATE PARALLEL HORIZONTAL LEGS, open on the RIGHT, connected by a semicircular bend at LEFT. EACH small stroke must have two free endpoints separated vertically by at least TWO stroke widths of clear transparent opening; neither may be a solid dash or closed oval. These two returns nest INSIDE the TWO larger bends of one separate winding reverse-S middle stroke. Make that middle section tall enough to preserve both U-turns clearly. The reference's THX specimen shows the coherent open/detached whole construction; compare all four to identify this character, then use that coherent construction without mixing merged alternatives. The right TOP has a bent-entry central upright crossed by TWO upward-open U arms, lower wider; its stem joins an outer horizontal roof that bends down into a long far-right side. Under that roof, the larger middle reverse-S startsupperLEFT, goesRIGHT, turnsDOWN and backLEFT, turnsDOWN and backRIGHT. Inside its upper pocket place the SMALL⊃, inside lower pocket the SMALL⊂; these are THREE independent middle writing strokes total. BOTTOM has a detached upright cup closed by a near-top crossbar with two tiny tips above it and exactly ONE enclosed counter. LEFT altar retains short detached upperdash, longer secondbar with long centralstem, and two detached long flank verticals. Keep all small and big winding strokes detached from each other and outer side; preserve white channels. Exactly one whole glyph, not a diagram.
Uniform width about2.7%canvas if needed to keep all specified gaps open. Do not replace any small return with a dash; all FOUR small parallel legs (two per return) must visibly exist.
